editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries changes the meaning, but a French technical editor would still change a few things. "Error mitigation" appears as "atténuation" in entries [15] and [26] but as "mitigation d'erreurs" in [19], even though "Atténue" is used in that same entry. Entry [19]'s "Atténue les valeurs d'espérance" reads as if the expectation values get smaller, not as if their errors are mitigated. Entry [26] still has linkText "Browse documentation" in English while [7] and [19] use "Parcourir la documentation", and the heading in [5] says "problèmes métier" while the paragraph under it ([6]) says "problèmes du domaine".

examples.source: Build custom error mitigation pipelines with techniques such as PEC, ZNE, and TREX

examples.suggested: Construis des pipelines personnalisés d'atténuation des erreurs
examples.why: Entries [15] and [26] use 'atténuation', and so does 'Atténue' in the PNA card of this same entry. Pick one term for the whole file.

examples.source: Mitigate expectation values by measuring a target observable that has absorbed noise model information.
examples.translation: Atténue les valeurs d'espérance en mesurant un observable cible…
examples.suggested: Atténue les erreurs sur les valeurs d'espérance en mesurant un observable cible…

examples.source: linkText="Browse documentation"
examples.translation: linkText="Browse documentation"

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, with a consistent "tu" register. "Context-based restrictions" is rendered as "restrictions contextuelles" throughout, and the role conditions in [5] (Administrateur/Éditeur/Observateur, "peut uniquement ajouter des zones réseau") match the source exactly.

examples.suggested: un job d'apprentissage du bruit distinct est nécessaire pour utiliser la PEA.

examples.source: Other notable options include:

editor_note: Entry 6 is accurate. Nothing is inverted, dropped or added, and it keeps the informal "te permet". A native editor would still fix a few calques. "une structure de données appelée un [Bloc Unifié de Primitive (PUB)]" copies the English article, and the English-style capitals read oddly in French. "la méthode run() pour la primitive Estimator" should say "de la primitive". "exécute la charge de travail définie comme un job" is a literal rendering of "as a job"; "sous forme de job" reads better. The closing phrase "options d'exécution spécifiées par la primitive" slightly shifts "specified from the primitive". It now suggests the primitive chooses the options, when the user sets them through the primitive.

examples.source: by using a data structure called a [**Primitive Unified Bloc (PUB)**]
examples.translation: en utilisant une structure de données appelée un [**Bloc Unifié de Primitive (PUB)**]
examples.suggested: à l'aide d'une structure de données appelée [**bloc unifié de primitive (PUB)**]
examples.why: 'appelée un' copies the English article, and French does not capitalize every word of a term like this.

examples.source: used as inputs to the run() method for the Estimator primitive, which executes the defined workload as a job
examples.translation: utilisés comme entrées pour la méthode run() pour la primitive Estimator, qui exécute la charge de travail définie comme un job
examples.suggested: utilisés comme entrées de la méthode run() de la primitive Estimator, qui exécute la charge de travail définie sous forme de job

examples.source: the runtime options specified from the primitive
examples.translation: des options d'exécution spécifiées par la primitive
examples.suggested: des options d'exécution spécifiées pour la primitive
examples.why: 'par la primitive' makes the primitive the one choosing the options. The user sets them, so this is a small shift in who does what, but it does not mislead.

editor_note: None of the 18 rewritten entries changes the meaning, so a learner would not be misled. Entry 25 says precision takes priority over options ("ont priorité sur"). Entry 36 keeps both the job-failure condition and the "inférieur au nombre de shots" comparison. Entries 20 and 32 keep their conditions ("n'a pas besoin d'être instanciée si", "True par défaut"), and the "Documentation API …" link labels are handled consistently. One wording fix: entry 25 calls the keyword argument "argument de mot-clé precision", a calque that French Python writers wouldn't use. "argument nommé `precision`" or "argument mot-clé `precision`" would be better. Entry 25 needs this fix; entry 26 (not in this delta) has the same wording and should change with it.

examples.source: and a precision keyword argument
examples.translation: et un argument de mot-clé precision
examples.suggested: et un argument nommé `precision`
examples.why: "argument de mot-clé" is a literal calque of "keyword argument". French Python writing uses "argument nommé" (or "argument mot-clé"), and the parameter name reads more clearly in code formatting. The meaning is right.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (4, 5, 6, 27) keep the English meaning. The client-side/server-side note, "remplacements directs", "le seul changement étant l'instruction d'import" and the tradeoff "compromis coût-précision" are all faithful, and the "tu" register holds. Entry 4 has two calques a native editor would change. "incluant le découplage dynamique…" reads as an anglicism where French would use "notamment" or "dont". "Les étapes de ce sujet" copies "this topic"; "de cette page" or "de ce guide" is more natural.

examples.source: including dynamical decoupling, Pauli-twirling, gate-folding ZNE, PEA, and PEC
examples.translation: incluant le découplage dynamique, le twirling de Pauli, le ZNE par repliement de gate, le PEA et le PEC
examples.suggested: notamment le découplage dynamique, le twirling de Pauli, le ZNE par repliement de gate, le PEA et le PEC
examples.why: "incluant" used as a present participle to introduce a list is an anglicism. "notamment" or "dont" is standard French technical style.

examples.source: The steps in this topic describe how to set up Estimator
examples.translation: Les étapes de ce sujet décrivent comment configurer Estimator
examples.suggested: Les étapes de cette page décrivent comment configurer Estimator
examples.why: "ce sujet" is a literal calque of the documentation term "topic". A French doc writer would refer to the page or guide.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Every caveat is kept: no simulator support yet, the guide covers Sampler only, shots apply to the whole job, and nothing is corrected implicitly. Three wording problems remain. In [13], "considérablement plus impliqué" copies the English "involved"; in French "impliqué" does not mean "complicated", so it should be "plus complexe/laborieux". In [89], the table row says "Annuler le brassage de mesure", but the rest of the file keeps "twirling" (for example "Annuler le twirling" in [32] and "twirling de mesure" in [64] and [93]), so the term is inconsistent. In [8], "à l'échelle utilitaire" is a stiff copy of "utility-scale".

examples.source: Migrating from Estimator to Executor is considerably more involved than migrating from Sampler
examples.translation: Migrer d'Estimator vers Executor est considérablement plus impliqué que de migrer depuis Sampler
examples.suggested: Migrer d'Estimator vers Executor est nettement plus complexe que de migrer depuis Sampler
examples.why: This copies 'involved' too literally. In French, 'impliqué' means 'implicated' or 'engaged', not 'complicated'.

examples.source: Undo measurement twirling
examples.translation: Annuler le brassage de mesure
examples.suggested: Annuler le twirling de mesure
examples.why: Everywhere else the file keeps 'twirling' ([32] 'Annuler le twirling', [64]/[93] 'twirling de mesure'). Switching to 'brassage' in one table row is inconsistent.

examples.source: runs utility-scale experiments
examples.translation: exécute des expériences à l'échelle utilitaire
examples.suggested: mène des expériences à l'échelle « utility »
examples.why: 'à l'échelle utilitaire' is a stiff word-for-word rendering. French technical writers usually keep 'utility-scale' or paraphrase it.

editor_note: Entry 7 is faithful and would not mislead a learner: the "these versions or newer" recommendation is kept exactly as "ces versions ou des versions plus récentes". The one problem is "développé avec les exigences suivantes", which calques "requirements". In this Python-package context, "exigences" sounds like functional specifications. A French technical writer would say "prérequis" or "dépendances" here.

examples.source: The code on this page was developed using the following requirements.
examples.translation: Le code de cette page a été développé avec les exigences suivantes.
examples.suggested: Le code de cette page a été développé avec les prérequis suivants.
examples.why: In a package-versions accordion, 'requirements' means software dependencies. 'Exigences' is a literal calque that reads like a specification document. 'Prérequis' or 'dépendances' is the idiomatic French term.

editor_note: Entry 19 is faithful and natural, and it keeps the caveat that the tuple `(input_dim, output_dim)` is "l'inverse de la forme de la matrice sous-jacente" with the order intact; it also uses the informal "tu peux utiliser" register.

All five rewritten entries are faithful. Entry 7 keeps the negation and the caveat intact ("ne peuvent pas se voir les uns les autres, même s'ils ont accès aux mêmes ressources"), entry 21 keeps "l'ensemble minimal de permissions", and entries 33 and 34 correctly localize "région us-east :" / "région eu-de :" in informal tu.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural French: [18] reads "Consulte ... pour tous les détails sur la classe", and [25] keeps the negation and the condition intact in "n'a pas besoin d'être instanciée si tu définis les options après l'initialisation de la primitive", with "tu" throughout.

Entry 7 is faithful and natural: it keeps the full list of what gets deleted ("tes jobs, résultats, paramètres et programmes"), renders "overflow menu" as "menu contextuel", leaves the UI label **Delete** in English, keeps the confirmation step and uses "tu" throughout.

The translation is faithful, and the terminology is correct and consistent throughout (tolérant aux fautes, théorème du seuil, valeur seuil, portes transversales), but some phrasing needs a native editor. In [2], "tant que trop peu de qubits sont affectés" is an awkward rendering of "so long as not too many qubits are affected", because "trop peu" suggests the number is too small. In [6], "soi-disant états magiques" sounds pejorative in French, and "les états dits magiques" is the neutral form. In [7], the emphatic "critically" before the key point that the threshold does *not* depend on circuit size was dropped, "composantes" should be "composants", and there are calques such as "il est connu que" in [5] and "discussion de haut niveau".

examples.source: so long as not too many qubits are affected
examples.translation: tant que trop peu de qubits sont affectés
examples.suggested: tant que le nombre de qubits affectés reste limité
examples.why: 'trop peu' means 'too few' and sounds like a shortfall, which is not what the English says. The phrase reads awkwardly and hides the intended condition (a limited number of errors).

examples.source: so-called *magic states*
examples.translation: les soi-disant *états magiques*
examples.suggested: les *états* dits *magiques*
examples.why: In French, 'soi-disant' suggests doubt or irony ('supposedly'), while the English only introduces a technical name.

examples.source: but critically it does *not* depend on the size of the quantum circuit
examples.translation: mais elle ne dépend *pas* de la taille du circuit quantique implémenté
examples.suggested: mais, point crucial, elle ne dépend *pas* de la taille du circuit quantique implémenté
examples.why: Dropping 'critically' weakens the emphasis on the most important point of the threshold theorem.

examples.source: the error rate for all of the components involved
examples.translation: le taux d'erreur de toutes les composantes impliquées
examples.suggested: le taux d'erreur de tous les composants impliqués
examples.why: Hardware or circuit parts are 'composants'. 'Composantes' means the components of a vector or a signal.

examples.source: But it is known that, as long as...
examples.translation: Mais il est connu que, tant que...
examples.suggested: On sait toutefois que, tant que...
examples.why: 'Il est connu que' is a calque of the English passive. A native technical writer would say 'on sait que'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall. Terms are correct and consistent (codes correcteurs d'erreurs quantiques, code torique, codes de surface, codes de couleur), and the "tu" register holds. There are two small problems. In [2], "isn't bad" becomes "n'est pas anodin" ("is not trivial"), so the sentence stresses difficulty rather than a modest but acceptable result; "n'est déjà pas mal" would keep the English tone. In [3], "jeter un premier regard sur" is a slightly stiff calque of "take a first look at".

examples.source: Correcting an error on one qubit out of five, seven, or nine isn't bad, but in all likelihood...
examples.translation: Corriger une erreur sur un qubit parmi cinq, sept ou neuf n'est pas anodin, mais il nous faudra très probablement...
examples.suggested: Corriger une erreur sur un qubit parmi cinq, sept ou neuf, ce n'est déjà pas mal, mais il nous faudra très probablement...
examples.why: 'n'est pas anodin' means 'is not trivial or insignificant', which changes the tone. The English calls this a modest, acceptable result, and the 'but' then sets it against the much higher tolerance needed.

examples.source: we'll take a first look at some more sophisticated quantum error correcting code constructions
examples.translation: nous allons jeter un premier regard sur des constructions de codes correcteurs d'erreurs quantiques plus sophistiquées
examples.suggested: nous allons découvrir des constructions plus sophistiquées de codes correcteurs d'erreurs quantiques
examples.why: 'jeter un premier regard sur' is a literal calque of 'take a first look at'. A native technical writer would say 'découvrir' or 'aborder'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful everywhere. That includes the square-root/square cost relation in [3], the hedged caveat in [5] ("semble peu susceptible", "sera inévitablement effacé") and the "slightly less than quadratic" claim in [6]. The one slip is in [6]: "fast sorting" is rendered as "les algorithmes de tri rapide (par exemple, le tri rapide et le tri fusion)". In French, "tri rapide" is the standard name for quicksort, so the phrase reads as if quicksort were a category that includes itself and merge sort. The "tu" register holds ("te guide", "Télécharge").

examples.source: including the fast Fourier transform and fast sorting (for example, quicksort and merge sort)
examples.translation: notamment la transformée de Fourier rapide et les algorithmes de tri rapide (par exemple, le tri rapide et le tri fusion)
examples.suggested: notamment la transformée de Fourier rapide et les algorithmes de tri efficaces (par exemple, le tri rapide et le tri fusion)
examples.why: 'Tri rapide' is the conventional French name for quicksort, so using it for the general category makes the example list circular and confusing.

editor_note: Entry 8 is faithful and natural. It uses the standard mathematical "Soient $\rho$ et $\sigma$ des matrices densité…", renders "fidelity" as "fidélité" as the rest of the page does, and leaves the formula and "(Tr)" unchanged.

Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful, "calcul quantique" is used consistently, and "tu" holds throughout. A native editor would still smooth a few calques: "offre des opportunités d'apprendre" in [0] and [4] copies the English "provides opportunities" word for word, and "l'état actuel et le futur" in [14] would read better as "l'avenir". In [17], "les étapes que tu peux franchir" is the wrong idiom for "steps you can take", since the meaning here is actions to take, not stages to get past.

examples.source: It provides opportunities to learn about potential industry applications
examples.translation: Elle offre des opportunités d'apprendre les applications industrielles potentielles
examples.suggested: Elle te permet de découvrir les applications industrielles potentielles
examples.why: This copies the English "provides opportunities to learn" word for word, and "apprendre les applications" is an awkward pairing. The same wording appears in entry [0].

examples.source: Understand the current state and future of quantum computing
examples.translation: Comprendre l'état actuel et le futur du calcul quantique
examples.suggested: Comprendre l'état actuel et l'avenir du calcul quantique
examples.why: When talking about where a field is heading, French uses "l'avenir". "Le futur" used as a noun here reads like a direct copy of the English.

examples.source: Identify the steps that you can take to become quantum ready
examples.translation: Identifier les étapes que tu peux franchir pour être prêt pour le quantique
examples.suggested: Identifier les mesures que tu peux prendre pour te préparer au quantique
examples.why: "Steps you can take" means actions to take here, not stages to get past, so "étapes à franchir" is the wrong idiom. "Être prêt pour le quantique" is also stiff.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing in it would mislead a learner. The 20-question count, the pass mark of at least 16, the lock after two failed attempts and the Credly privacy notice are all kept, and the informal "tu" register holds. Entry [8] has a grammar slip: "tu dois en répondre correctement au moins 16" misuses the pronoun "en", because "répondre" takes "à" ("répondre à une question"). In [12], "réclamer ton badge" is a calque of "claim". A French writer would use "récupérer".

examples.source: you must answer at least 16 correctly to pass
examples.translation: tu dois en répondre correctement au moins 16 pour réussir
examples.suggested: tu dois répondre correctement à au moins 16 d'entre elles pour réussir
examples.why: "Répondre" takes "à", so the pronoun "en" is ungrammatical here and reads as a calque of the English.

examples.source: instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: les instructions pour réclamer ton badge
examples.suggested: les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: "Réclamer" suggests demanding something owed. For a badge, "récupérer" is the natural French verb.

editor_note: Entry 21, the Credly privacy notice, is faithful: the shared data (nom, adresse e-mail, badge obtenu), US location, global sharing and the IBM privacy links all match the English, so it would not mislead anyone. A native editor would still change three things. "processeur de données tiers" is a calque of "data processor"; the standard French privacy/GDPR term is "sous-traitant (de données)". "réclamer le badge" and "t'émettre" are calques too, and "récupérer ton badge" and "te délivrer" read more naturally. The sentence-final period has also been moved inside both link labels ("[ici.]").

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: un processeur de données tiers autorisé par IBM
examples.suggested: un sous-traitant de données tiers autorisé par IBM
examples.why: In French data-protection language a 'data processor' is a 'sous-traitant'. 'Processeur' sounds like hardware.

examples.source: In order to issue you an IBM Digital Badge ... instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: Afin de t'émettre un IBM Digital Badge ... les instructions pour réclamer le badge
examples.suggested: Afin de te délivrer un IBM Digital Badge ... les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: 'Réclamer' suggests demanding something or making a complaint, and 'émettre' is a calque. 'Délivrer' and 'récupérer' are the idiomatic choices.

examples.source: can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.translation: peut être consultée [ici.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/)
examples.suggested: peut être consultée [ici](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.why: The period has moved inside the link text, which leaves a period inside the link label. Keep the source punctuation outside the link.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (43, 48, 49, 50, 60) changes the meaning, so nothing here would mislead a learner. There is one naturalness problem, in entry 49. "faire une très bonne hypothèse pour ton ansatz qui a un excellent chevauchement…" is a word-for-word copy of the English "make a very good guess for your ansatz". A French writer would say "deviner un très bon ansatz" or "bien choisir ton ansatz" instead. The same entry would also read more naturally with "s'accompagne de garanties" than with "est accompagné de garanties". Entries 43, 48, 50 and 60 are faithful and read naturally. They use "tu" consistently, and "test de Hadamard" and "temps QPU" are correct.

examples.source: In SQD you either need to make a very good guess for your ansatz that has excellent overlap with the ground state support in the computational basis
examples.translation: Dans SQD, tu dois soit faire une très bonne hypothèse pour ton ansatz qui a un excellent chevauchement avec le support de l'état fondamental dans la base computationnelle
examples.suggested: Avec SQD, tu dois soit deviner un très bon ansatz, dont le chevauchement avec le support de l'état fondamental dans la base computationnelle est excellent
examples.why: This copies the English phrase "make a guess for" word for word. "Faire une hypothèse pour ton ansatz" is stiff and slightly off in French: the ansatz is chosen or guessed, not the object of a hypothesis.

editor_note: Entry 48 is faithful and reads naturally. "Vrai ou faux ? Les états quantiques hautement intriqués nous permettent de résoudre la plupart des problèmes d'apprentissage automatique plus efficacement" keeps "most" as "la plupart", keeps the comparative, and matches the answer "Faux" in entry 49. "Intriqués" is also consistent with "intrication" and "états intriqués" elsewhere in the file.

The meaning is accurate throughout. The four techniques (suppression, atténuation, détection, correction des erreurs), the "combined vs. conflicting" emphasis and the note about the exam and badge being released progressively all match the English. The one defect is the page description in [0], which opens with the formal imperative "Découvrez" and breaks the informal "tu" convention. It should read "Découvre". Everything else is written with "nous" and has no register problem.

examples.source: Explore modern tools for handling noise and errors to get the most out of quantum computers.
examples.translation: Découvrez des outils modernes pour gérer le bruit et les erreurs afin de tirer le meilleur parti des ordinateurs quantiques.
examples.suggested: Découvre des outils modernes pour gérer le bruit et les erreurs afin de tirer le meilleur parti des ordinateurs quantiques.
examples.why: The formal vous-imperative breaks the informal tu convention the project requires.

editor_note: None of the 13 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The meaning holds throughout: the T1 decay and rock analogy (187), the oblate spheroid that shrinks less in XY than along Z (205/207), the case where p→1 restores coherence (227), and the two-qubit transpiled depth metric (253). A few phrasings still read like calques. In 100, "retourner erronément un 0" is stiff. In 218, "reste transformé vers la surface" and "le long du plan XY" (from "across the XY plane") read like English syntax. In 227, "une chance de 50-50" is also a calque. The tu register and the terms (matrice de densité, canal de relaxation énergétique, déphasage, portes SWAP) are correct and used the same way throughout.

examples.source: each qubit need not be equally likely to erroneously return a 0 and to erroneously return a 1
examples.translation: chaque qubit n'a pas nécessairement la même probabilité de retourner erronément un 0 et de retourner erronément un 1
examples.suggested: chaque qubit n'a pas nécessairement la même probabilité de renvoyer à tort un 0 que de renvoyer à tort un 1
examples.why: 'retourner erronément' is stiff translationese; 'renvoyer à tort' is the idiomatic phrasing.

examples.source: are still mapped to the sphere's surface ... a shrinking of the shaded region across the XY plane
examples.translation: reste transformé vers la surface de la sphère ... une contraction de la région ombrée le long du plan XY
examples.suggested: reste envoyé sur la surface de la sphère ... une contraction de la région ombrée dans le plan XY
examples.why: 'transformé vers' and 'le long du plan' are calques; a map sends a state 'sur' the surface, and a contraction happens 'dans le plan'.

examples.source: correspond to a 50-50 chance of a phase error occurring
examples.translation: corresponde à une chance de 50-50 qu'une erreur de phase se produise
examples.suggested: corresponde à une probabilité de 50 % qu'une erreur de phase se produise
examples.why: 'chance de 50-50' is an English idiom carried over literally; French technical prose would give the probability.

editor_note: The four short prose entries are faithful and natural, e.g. "Le module est hébergé sur GitHub" and "peut être considérée comme optionnelle, mais est fortement recommandée", which keeps the optional-but-recommended caveat.

Entries 32, 33 and 36 say the same thing as the English. They keep the degree-4 star vs degree-3 heavy-hex argument, the point that SWAP routing raises the gate count, and the caveat that the Qiskit transpiler has no GHZ synthesis. Nothing here would mislead a learner. In entry 33, one sentence uses both the calque "graphe de couplage hexagonal lourd" and "graphe de couplage heavy-hex" for the same lattice, and French quantum writers usually keep "heavy-hex". Entry 36 has two stiff calques: "circuit exemple jouet" and "comme montré ci-dessus", where the past participle should agree with "synthèse".

examples.source: so on IBM® Brisbane's heavy-hexagon coupling graph as well ... cannot be laid out on the heavy-hex coupling graph
examples.translation: et donc aussi sur le graphe de couplage hexagonal lourd d'IBM® Brisbane ... sur le graphe de couplage heavy-hex
examples.suggested: et donc aussi sur le graphe de couplage heavy-hex d'IBM® Brisbane ... sur ce graphe heavy-hex, dont les nœuds sont au plus de degré 3

examples.source: manual circuit synthesis as shown above ... using the following toy example circuit
examples.translation: la synthèse manuelle de circuit comme montré ci-dessus ... à l'aide du circuit exemple jouet suivant
examples.suggested: une synthèse manuelle de circuit comme celle présentée ci-dessus ... à l'aide du petit circuit d'exemple suivant

editor_note: Entry 64 is faithful and reads naturally. It renders "fake backend" as "backend fictif", "baseline Trotter circuit" as "circuit de Trotter de référence" and "observable ZZ" the same way as entry 62, and it keeps "for each" as "pour chacun".

The meaning is faithful throughout. The RZZ angle bounds, the list of unsupported features (PEC, ZNE/PEA), the two workflow approaches and the "almost identical" QPU-time claim all carry over, and "portes fractionnaires" and "passe de transpilation" are used consistently. The problems are small and a native editor would still fix them. "Qiskit patterns" appears as "modèles Qiskit" in [9], "pattern standard de Qiskit" in [57] and the untranslated "Qiskit patterns" everywhere else. [95] writes "appliquons le transpiler" instead of "transpileur". [16] uses "certaines unitaires" as a bare noun, [4] and [50] are calques, and [38] "Requirements" becomes "Prérequis", the same title as the [10] heading.

examples.source: keeping the standard Qiskit patterns workflow

examples.suggested: le flux de travail standard Qiskit patterns
examples.why: Elsewhere the file keeps 'Qiskit patterns' ([27], [54], [65], [84]), and [57] uses 'pattern standard de Qiskit'. That is three renderings of the same framework name.

examples.source: we apply the transpiler using `constructor-beta` translation

examples.translation: tu peux implémenter certaines unitaires plus efficacement
examples.suggested: tu peux implémenter certaines opérations unitaires plus efficacement
examples.why: 'unitaires' is not used as a bare feminine noun in French; it needs a head noun (opérations or opérateurs).

examples.source: we refer to this value as the *fidelity*, defined as

examples.suggested: Objectifs d'apprentissage

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. I found no inverted conditions, and the variational-bound, M_J-on-products and qubit-excitation arguments all survive intact. The register flips partway through the page: entries [0]–[102] use vous ("Regroupez", "Apprenez", "Vous avez également besoin", "Soumettez"), while [104] onward switch to the required tu ("Convertis", "Utilise", "tu peux"). Several key terms also switch rendering in the second half: pool is "réservoir" and then "pool", workflow is "workflow" and then "flux de travail", the method name is "pooled SQD" and then "SQD groupé", and the article before hamiltonien switches from "l'hamiltonien" to "le hamiltonien".

examples.source: Pool nuclear Slater determinants ...
examples.translation: Regroupez les déterminants de Slater nucléaires ... diagonalisez l'hamiltonien
examples.suggested: Regroupe les déterminants de Slater nucléaires ... diagonalise l'hamiltonien

examples.suggested: Le workflow pooled SQD publié

examples.translation: il y a un problème avec le hamiltonien
examples.suggested: il y a un problème avec l'hamiltonien
examples.why: This entry uses 'le hamiltonien', but earlier entries ([0], [22], [33]) elide the article to 'l'hamiltonien'. The page should pick one form.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The QUBO formulation, the x_j=1→région A / x_j=0→région B assignment and the options description (shots, transpile_only, job_tags) all match the source. There are three small slips. Entry [3] switches to the formal register ("Votre temps d'exécution") while the rest of the file uses "tu". Entry [42] leaves "problème Market Split" in English, although every other entry says "problème de répartition de marché". The heading "Résultats d'apprentissage" is a calque of "Learning outcomes"; "Objectifs d'apprentissage" is the usual French wording.

examples.translation: Votre temps d'exécution peut varier.
examples.suggested: Ton temps d'exécution peut varier.

examples.source: Learning outcomes

editor_note: I only judged the four rewritten entries. None of them would mislead a learner, and entries 0, 33 and 55 are faithful and natural ("l'encodage par corrélation de Pauli", "s'écrit :", tu-register "Si ce travail t'a plu"). Entry 7 needs a small edit. "matériel quantique à court terme" is a stiff calque of "near-term", and "(NISQ)" is a gloss the English does not have. Entry 12 already renders the same idea as "dispositifs quantiques actuels", so the two entries should match.

examples.source: Implement PCE in practice to encode and solve large‑scale optimization tasks on near‑term quantum hardware.
examples.translation: Mettre en œuvre le PCE en pratique pour encoder et résoudre des tâches d'optimisation à grande échelle sur du matériel quantique à court terme (NISQ).
examples.suggested: Mettre en œuvre le PCE en pratique pour encoder et résoudre des tâches d'optimisation à grande échelle sur le matériel quantique actuel.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. The numbers, conditions and caveats all survive intact: γ²=100 vs ≈6.3 and the ~16x reduction, the rule that a sample is discarded only if both qubits fail, the 1/((1-α)(1-β)) overhead, and the residual bias below 0.01. Terms are consistent: valeurs moyennes, couches d'intrication, post-sélection, élaguer, surcoût d'échantillonnage, and 'tu' is used throughout. A native editor would still smooth two phrasings: the rare calque 'médier l'intrication' in [17], and the notation '16x' in [35], where French typically writes '16×' or 'd'un facteur 16'.

examples.source: mediating entanglement between the Ising qubits
examples.translation: médier l'intrication entre les qubits d'Ising
examples.suggested: servir d'intermédiaires pour l'intrication entre les qubits d'Ising
examples.why: 'Médier' is a rare, stiff calque of 'mediate'. A French technical writer would use a periphrasis instead.

examples.source: roughly a 16x reduction
examples.translation: soit une réduction d'environ 16x
examples.suggested: soit une réduction d'un facteur 16 environ
examples.why: The '16x' notation is English typographic usage. In French prose, 'd'un facteur 16' (or '16×') reads more naturally.

editor_note: None of the 7 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Negations, quantities and caveats all carry over, including the 80-minute QPU runtime, the precomputed projections and the "potentially" hedge in [11]. Three small wording problems remain. In [52] and [56], "radial basis function kernel" becomes "fonction de noyau à base radiale", which mixes up the usual French term; "noyau à fonction de base radiale (RBF)" is the standard form. In [52], "Cela est dû à la fonction … disponible directement" copies the English "This is due to" word for word. In [11], the process "feature mapping" is named with the noun "carte de caractéristiques", which does not describe a process.

examples.source: This is due to the readily available radial basis function (``'rbf'``) kernel
examples.translation: Cela est dû à la fonction de noyau à base radiale (``'rbf'``) disponible directement
examples.suggested: Cela tient au fait que le noyau à fonction de base radiale (``'rbf'``) y est directement disponible
examples.why: The usual French term is 'noyau à fonction de base radiale (RBF)'. 'Cela est dû à' is also a word-for-word copy of 'This is due to'.

examples.source: a classical SVM with the radial basis function as the kernel
examples.translation: un SVM classique avec la fonction de noyau à base radiale
examples.suggested: un SVM classique utilisant comme noyau la fonction de base radiale (RBF)
examples.why: This has the same term problem as [52]. The radial basis function is itself the kernel; it is not a 'kernel function with a radial base'.

examples.source: typically through a process called feature mapping
examples.translation: généralement par un processus appelé carte de caractéristiques (feature mapping)
examples.suggested: généralement au moyen d'une carte de caractéristiques (feature map), c'est-à-dire d'un plongement
examples.why: The English names a process, but the French gives it the name of an object (the map). The meaning is still clear, so this is minor.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the caveats in [118]/[119] and the median-rate caveat in [108]. I found no drift and nothing that would mislead a learner. A native technical editor would still change a few things. "Observable" switches gender: it is feminine in [18]/[22] and masculine in [6], [36], [117] and [125]. "Workflow" and "flux de travail" alternate, and so do "le PNA" and a bare "PNA". The title term shows up as both "absorption de bruit propagée" and "propagé" ([6]). Some calques also remain: "restaure déjà la valeur d'espérance proche du benchmark idéal" ([149]), "se rapprochant presque" ([152]) and "n'est pas garanti d'être monotone" ([118]).

examples.source: Construct a mirrored Trotterized kicked-Ising model and a target observable.
examples.translation: Construire un modèle d'Ising kické Trotterisé et miroité ainsi qu'un observable cible.
examples.suggested: Construire un modèle d'Ising pulsé (kicked Ising), trotterisé et miroir, ainsi qu'une observable cible.
examples.why: 'Observable' is masculine here and in [117]/[125], but feminine in [18]/[22] ('l'observable elle-même'). The file should use one gender, preferably the feminine.

examples.source: The plain PNA approach already restores the expectation value close to the ideal benchmark
examples.translation: L'approche PNA simple restaure déjà la valeur d'espérance proche du benchmark idéal
examples.suggested: L'approche PNA seule ramène déjà la valeur d'espérance près de la référence idéale
examples.why: This is a calque of 'restores ... close to'. 'restaure ... proche' is not idiomatic French.

examples.source: yields the most accurate result, nearly matching the ideal value
examples.translation: donne le résultat le plus précis, se rapprochant presque de la valeur idéale
examples.suggested: donne le résultat le plus précis, quasiment égal à la valeur idéale
examples.why: 'se rapprochant presque' is redundant and awkward. The English says the result nearly matches the ideal value.

examples.source: What propagated noise absorption (PNA) is
examples.translation: Ce qu'est l'absorption de bruit propagé (PNA)
examples.suggested: Ce qu'est l'absorption de bruit propagée (PNA)
examples.why: The technique's name is rendered 'bruit propagé' here and 'bruit propagée' in [0], [1], [16] and [17]. The name should be spelled the same way throughout.

examples.source: but this behavior is not guaranteed to be monotonic.
examples.translation: mais ce comportement n'est pas garanti d'être monotone.
examples.suggested: mais rien ne garantit que ce comportement soit monotone.
examples.why: This is an English passive calque. It is not idiomatic in French.

editor_note: Entry 76 is faithful and natural in the informal "tu" register ("mets tes compétences à l'épreuve", "Documentation sur la transpilation … pour affiner l'optimisation des circuits", "Suppression et atténuation des erreurs"), and all four recommendations keep their meaning.

The five rewritten entries (13, 27, 42, 51, 66) keep the English meaning and would not mislead a learner. Entry 27 has a gender-agreement error: "tous les 4 orbitales spatiales" should read "toutes les quatre orbitales spatiales", because "orbitale" is feminine. In entry 51, "heuristique de scoring" is an anglicism and "d'évaluation" is more natural. Also in entry 51, "Si toutes les paires ne peuvent pas être implémentées" leans toward the reading "if no pair can be implemented", so "Si certaines paires ne peuvent pas être implémentées" would state the condition unambiguously.

examples.source: a connection between orbitals of different spin is present at every 4th spatial orbital
examples.translation: une connexion entre les orbitales de spin différent est présente tous les 4 orbitales spatiales
examples.suggested: une connexion entre orbitales de spins différents est présente toutes les quatre orbitales spatiales
examples.why: "Orbitale" is feminine, so "tous les" is an agreement error. "De spin différent" also reads better as "de spins différents".

examples.source: If not all pairs can be implemented, it emits a warning.
examples.translation: Si toutes les paires ne peuvent pas être implémentées, elle émet un avertissement.
examples.suggested: Si certaines paires ne peuvent pas être implémentées, elle émet un avertissement.
examples.why: "Toutes ... ne ... pas" is ambiguous in French and can be read as "none of the pairs". "Certaines" matches the English condition exactly.

examples.source: This function uses a scoring heuristic
examples.translation: Cette fonction utilise une heuristique de scoring
examples.suggested: Cette fonction utilise une heuristique d'évaluation (de notation)
examples.why: "Scoring" is an unnecessary anglicism because standard French equivalents exist. Starting the paragraph with "Comme" instead of "Parce que" would also read more naturally.

editor_note: The physics is carried over faithfully: KCuF3, the factor-of-2 J normalization, zero ground-state magnetization and the fidelity numbers at the 50-qubit scale all match the English, and "tu" is used throughout. There is no semantic drift. The main problem is in [62], where "étape" translates both the time "steps" and the optimization "stages", so the warm-start and reset rule becomes muddled. Two terms are also rendered two ways: "Pauli twirling" is "twirling de Pauli" in [74] but "brouillage de Pauli" in [75] and [88], and AQC is "compilation quantique approximative" in [6] but "approchée" everywhere else. A few calques remain: "Résultats d'apprentissage" in [8], "temps d'horloge murale" in [73], and the doubled "en utilisant" in [48].

examples.source: The first $k_1$ steps use the one-layer ansatz and the next $k_2$ steps use the two-layer ansatz; within each stage, each step warm-starts from the previous step's optimized parameters, and parameters are reset to the stage defaults at the stage boundary.
examples.translation: Les $k_1$ premières étapes utilisent l'ansatz à une couche et les $k_2$ étapes suivantes utilisent l'ansatz à deux couches ; au sein de chaque étape, chaque pas démarre à chaud ... aux valeurs par défaut de l'étape à la limite de celle-ci.
examples.suggested: Les $k_1$ premiers pas utilisent l'ansatz à une couche et les $k_2$ pas suivants l'ansatz à deux couches ; au sein de chaque phase, chaque pas démarre à chaud à partir des paramètres optimisés du pas précédent, et les paramètres sont réinitialisés aux valeurs par défaut de la phase lors du passage d'une phase à l'autre.
examples.why: 'étape' is used for both steps and stages, which blurs the distinction the reset rule depends on; 'phase' keeps the stage concept separate, and 'pas' matches how steps are rendered elsewhere.

examples.source: QPU with DD, Pauli twirling, and TREX
examples.translation: QPU avec DD, brouillage de Pauli et TREX
examples.suggested: QPU avec DD, twirling de Pauli et TREX
examples.why: [74] uses 'twirling de Pauli' and TREX is glossed as 'par twirling', so the same technique ends up with two names (also 'brouillage' in [88]).

examples.source: approximate quantum compiling (AQC)
examples.translation: la compilation quantique approximative (AQC)
examples.suggested: la compilation quantique approchée (AQC)
examples.why: Every other occurrence ([11], [37], [38], [57], [89]) uses 'approchée'.

examples.source: To reduce the wall-clock time
examples.translation: Pour réduire le temps d'horloge murale
examples.suggested: Pour réduire le temps d'exécution réel
examples.why: 'temps d'horloge murale' is a literal calque; French technical writing says 'temps réel écoulé' or 'temps d'exécution réel'.

examples.source: Learning outcomes
examples.translation: Résultats d'apprentissage
examples.suggested: Objectifs d'apprentissage
examples.why: 'Objectifs d'apprentissage' is the conventional French heading for this section.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The caveats on postselection rate, shot budget scaling and unbiased-but-coarser estimation are all kept. The problems are consistency and polish. "payload" is left as "payload" in [14]-[37] but becomes "charge utile" from [41] onward. Ancilla appears as "ancillaires", "ancilles" and "ancilla(s)", and the spelling switches between "post-sélection" and "postsélection". [60] says "portes intriquées" (entangled gates) where [17] correctly says "portes intriquantes". There is also a gender agreement slip in [63] ("presque toutes les échantillons"). [70] "également bruitée" can be read as "also noisy" rather than "equally noisy".

examples.source: Each check uses entangling gates between one ancilla and one target.
examples.translation: Chaque vérification utilise des portes intriquées entre une ancilla et une cible.
examples.suggested: Chaque vérification utilise des portes intriquantes entre une ancilla et une cible.
examples.why: 'Entangling' means the gates create entanglement, not that the gates are entangled. [17] already uses 'portes intriquantes'.

examples.source: when the checks detect nearly all erroneous samples
examples.translation: lorsque les vérifications détectent presque toutes les échantillons erronés
examples.suggested: lorsque les vérifications détectent presque tous les échantillons erronés
examples.why: 'Échantillon' is masculine, so this is a gender agreement error.

examples.source: The payload circuit is a shallow one-dimensional brickwork random Clifford circuit.
examples.translation: Le circuit de charge utile est un circuit de Clifford brickwork aléatoire...
examples.suggested: Choose one rendering for 'payload' (e.g. 'charge utile') and use it everywhere, including [14], [15], [17] and [37], where it is left as 'payload'.
examples.why: The same key concept has two different names in one file.

examples.source: rather than assuming every edge is equally noisy
examples.translation: plutôt que de supposer que chaque arête est également bruitée
examples.suggested: plutôt que de supposer que toutes les arêtes sont aussi bruitées les unes que les autres
examples.why: 'Également' can mean 'also'. The intended meaning is 'equally noisy'.

examples.source: Small-scale simulator example
examples.translation: Exemple de simulateur à petite échelle
examples.suggested: Exemple à petite échelle sur simulateur
examples.why: The French reads as if the simulator itself is small-scale. The suggested wording also matches the heading in [68] ('Exemple à grande échelle sur matériel').

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the hard caveats in [59] (the filtering changes the evolved operator, and the qDRIFT bounds then apply to the filtered operator) and in [87]–[93]. The tu register holds. The problems are wording, not meaning. The article before Hamiltonian changes mid-file: "le hamiltonien" in [16]–[29], then "l'hamiltonien" from [44] on. [50] has the ungrammatical "dont échantillonne le protocole qDRIFT". In [92], "plus ou moins de sept 1" reads idiomatically as "roughly seven", which clashes with the intended "anything other than seven" (context saves it). A few other phrasings are stiff ("Exemple de simulateur", "Résultats d'apprentissage", "avant de terminer le post-traitement").

examples.source: any bitstrings that have more or fewer than seven 1s in the first and the second half
examples.translation: toute chaîne de bits comportant plus ou moins de sept 1
examples.suggested: toute chaîne de bits dont la première ou la seconde moitié ne comporte pas exactement sept 1
examples.why: 'plus ou moins' in French usually means 'roughly', so the sentence can be misread as discarding strings with about seven 1s. The surrounding context disambiguates it, but the phrasing is ambiguous.

examples.source: the operator coefficient distribution which the qDRIFT protocol samples from
examples.translation: la distribution des coefficients de l'opérateur dont échantillonne le protocole qDRIFT
examples.suggested: la distribution des coefficients de l'opérateur dans laquelle le protocole qDRIFT effectue ses tirages
examples.why: 'dont échantillonne' is ungrammatical because 'échantillonner' does not take 'de'. It reads as a calque of 'samples from'.

examples.source: Loading the Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Chargement de l'hamiltonien
examples.suggested: Pick one elision convention for the whole file, e.g. 'du hamiltonien' / 'le hamiltonien' as in [16]-[29]
examples.why: Entries [16]-[29] use 'le hamiltonien' (aspirated h) and entries [44]-[88] use 'l'hamiltonien'. Both forms exist, but mixing them in one page is inconsistent.

examples.source: We convert them to boolean vectors before finally post-processing with SQD.
examples.translation: Nous les convertissons en vecteurs booléens avant de terminer le post-traitement avec SQD.
examples.suggested: Nous les convertissons en vecteurs booléens avant le post-traitement final avec SQD.
examples.why: 'avant de terminer le post-traitement' means 'before finishing the post-processing', which slightly shifts the English 'before finally post-processing'.

examples.source: Simulator example
examples.translation: Exemple de simulateur
examples.suggested: Exemple sur simulateur
examples.why: 'Exemple de simulateur' means an example of a simulator. The parallel heading [85] correctly uses 'Exemple sur matériel'.
